slides.title: Google's new cart puts you next to Target
slides.sub: Universal Cart lets shoppers fill one cart from many stores in Search and Gemini. Here's what it means for your brand.

slides.title: What launched
slides.body: Universal Cart went live in the US on October 15 in Google Search, including AI Mode, and the Gemini app. Shoppers save items from many stores.

slides.title: What the cart does
slides.body: It tracks price drops and restocks, shows promo codes, and lets shoppers pay with Google Pay or send the cart to the store's own site.

slides.title: Listings in the mix
slides.body: Universal Cart pulls from more than 60 billion product listings in Google's Shopping Graph. Your product has to stand out in that crowd.

slides.title: Who's in already
slides.body: Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair and many Shopify merchants. You stay the seller of record on every order.

slides.title: Your listing is your storefront
slides.body: In one cart, your product sits right beside the big names. Clear photos, plain product names and a logo people recognize do the selling.

slides.title: Your site still closes it
slides.body: Shoppers can move the cart to your website to check out. It has to load fast, look like your brand and make paying easy.

slides.title: Make your products ready for Google's new cart
slides.body: We design brand identities, product visuals and fast, SEO-ready websites for Black-owned businesses, so you hold your own next to the biggest stores.

caption:
Google Universal Cart checklist: 4 things Black-owned businesses that sell online should have ready now that Google lets shoppers mix stores in one cart.

Google launched Universal Cart in the US on October 15. It works in Google Search, including AI Mode, and in the Gemini app. Shoppers can save products from different stores in one cart, get alerts on price drops and restocks, see promo codes, and pay with Google Pay or move the cart to the store's own site. Early partners include Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair and many Shopify merchants, and the store stays the seller of record.

Here's what to have in place:
1. Product photos that look sharp and consistent at thumbnail size.
2. Plain, searchable product names and descriptions.
3. A logo and brand look shoppers recognize in a lineup.
4. A fast website with an easy checkout for carts sent your way.

If you sell on Shopify, check Sales channels > Agentic in your admin to see your settings.
